title: Assertion Creation (2)
code:
CREATE ASSERTION smallClub
    CHECK
    ((SELECT COUNT(S.sid) 
     FROM sailor S) + 
    (SELECT COUNT(B.sid) 
     FROM boats B)
      < 100));

lines.explanation: The previous example ('Assertion Creation (1)') checks the values within itself and it is inappropriate. This example explains ASSERTION as the right solution; not associated with either table. An ASSERTION is a database constraint that restricts the contents of the database as a whole. Like a CHECK constraint, an assertion is specified as a search condition. But the difference of ASSERTION with CHECK constraint is that the search condition in an assertion can restrict the contents of multiple tables and the data relationships among them. For that reaon, an ASSERTION is specified as part of the overall database definition, via CREATE ASSERTION statement.
'CHECK' keyword is mandantory for creating assertion.
In this example,  both sailor and boats are target tables to be compared as a search condition. This returns the number of sailors.
Two query results are summed up.
This query counts the number of boats.
The summed result of two queries is compared with 100 and checks if the value is less than 100.
